description: Topic-only bucket (no question text) so the interviewer can attack from any angle and drill deeper based on answer quality. sampling_weight = frequency_score x recency_multiplier; used for weighted random selection at runtime (never zero probability).

fundamentals.why_it_matters: Tests understanding of first-class functions and closures, not just 'put @ before a function'. Real depth: writing one with arguments, decorator chaining/order.
Underpins decorators and callback patterns. Good follow-up: late-binding closure bugs in loops.
Tests memory-efficiency reasoning, not just syntax. Follow-up: when NOT to use a generator (e.g. need multiple passes).

Separates people who've only used Python from people who understand its runtime. Follow-up: why GIL doesn't block multiprocessing. Recency boosted — free-threaded (no-GIL) Python builds are an active, current topic.

fundamentals.topic: Threading vs Multiprocessing vs AsyncIO — when to use which
fundamentals.why_it_matters: CPU-bound vs I/O-bound reasoning. Common real-world backend question, not academic trivia. Async is increasingly default in modern backend frameworks.
Classic real bug (mutable default persists across calls). Tests if they've actually been bitten by it.
Quick filter question, but has a real follow-up about small-int/string interning caching behavior.
Nested mutable objects are a real source of production bugs — good scenario-based follow-up potential.
Simple on the surface; follow-up into argument unpacking and API design (flexible function signatures) adds depth.
Tests whether they understand variable resolution, not just 'global vs local'.

fundamentals.topic: Context managers and the with statement
fundamentals.why_it_matters: Follow-up: writing a custom context manager with __enter__/__exit__ or contextlib. Directly relevant to backend resource handling (DB connections, files).
Follow-up: implementing __eq__, __hash__, __repr__ correctly together — a common real mistake.
Tests Python's dynamic-typing philosophy vs static-typed languages — good comparative discussion topic.
Advanced filter question for senior candidates — most won't need it daily but understanding it signals depth.
Bridges into performance/optimization discussion and ties naturally into a live-coding follow-up.

fundamentals.topic: OOP — inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation in practice
fundamentals.why_it_matters: Ask for real examples/tradeoffs, not definitions — this is where shallow-prep candidates get caught.

fundamentals.topic: Exception handling — try/except/else/finally and custom exceptions
fundamentals.why_it_matters: Follow-up: exception hierarchy design for a real API (when to create custom exception classes).
Good discussion topic: when it's a legitimate testing tool (mocking) vs a dangerous production anti-pattern. Slightly less commonly asked directly compared to other hard topics here.

fundamentals.topic: FastAPI Event Loop Blocking with psycopg2
fundamentals.why_it_matters: Crucial for your target stack. Tests if you know that blocking sync code inside an async def endpoint halts the entire server process, and how thread pools fix it.

fundamentals.topic: Memory Overhead: fetchall() vs Server-side Named Cursors
fundamentals.why_it_matters: Tests production data scaling awareness. Explores how streaming huge query responses directly from PostgreSQL prevents Python memory crashes.
